newsitem.title: USA: Oregon moves closer to budget deal, bond on ballot.
newsitem.headline: Oregon moves closer to budget deal, bond on ballot.

text.p: Oregon's legislature moved closer to a budget deal Friday, but after failing to agree to school construction funding, it decided to put a $150 million bond measure on the November ballot.
The 17 negotiators, joined by Gov. John Kitzhaber, reached an agreement late Thursday night on about $9.6 billion in state funding for 1997-99.
Senate leadership signed off on the deal Friday morning, and the House leadership was expected to do so shortly.
The full Senate and the House still must approve the budget. They are expected to discuss it next week.

The state's fiscal year begins July 1, but if the measure is not approved by then, a continuing resolution is already in the works to keep state-operated institutions running, according to Barbara Crocker, an official in Senate President Brady Adams' office.
Included in the package is a $150 million bond measure for school improvements that will be sent to voters Nov. 4.
The House wanted the bond measure to be included in the budget, but the Senate did not, hence the compromise to seek voter approval of the measure.
School funding was one of the most contentious issues in the budget package and was agreed to at $4.2 billion. That boosts average per pupil spending to about $4,500 per year, up from $4,256.

A controversial transportation tax package, which the Senate killed two weeks ago, was not part of the budget deal, but still may be enacted. Separately legislators were working on a new 6-cent-a-gallon gas tax and increased vehicle registration fees to fund road construction.
